expect:
Quality of written communication assessed.
Top band (9-12): Detailed and well-organised comparison with accurate musical vocabulary. Clear references to specific examples. Addresses all three areas (forces, texture, purpose) with well-developed points.
Mid band (5-8): Sound comparison with some musical vocabulary. May not address all three areas in equal depth. Some reference to examples.
Lower band (1-4): Basic comparison with limited musical vocabulary. May describe one ensemble without comparing. Few or no specific examples.
Indicative content:
• Forces: Musical theatre uses voices (soloists, duets, chorus) as lead instruments plus a pit band; chamber music uses only instruments (e.g. string quartet: 2 violins, viola, cello)
• Texture: Musical theatre has the widest range of textural contrasts (solo voice to full chorus + orchestra); chamber music textures are typically homophonic or polyphonic within a small group
• Purpose: Musical theatre tells a story and expresses character emotions; chamber music is abstract and focuses on musical development
• Style: Musical theatre may mix pop, jazz, and classical styles; chamber music is rooted in the Western classical tradition
• Examples: Defying Gravity (Wicked) — dramatic build from solo to full ensemble; Mozart String Quartet K.157 — instruments share melodic material equally
